_comment: DEF200 — async handlers the census flags as reaching sync I/O. Frozen 2026-08-18 (AT:R70) at 87; swept to 38 on 2026-08-25 (plain `def`), narrowed to 21 on 2026-08-28 (call vs mention), and CLEARED to 0 on 2026-11-22 (AT:B1) by wrapping every remaining blocking call in asyncio.to_thread / run_in_threadpool. The list is empty on purpose and may only stay empty: do not add an entry to get a build past the guard. READ `total_async_handlers_when_frozen` TOGETHER WITH THIS: the flagged count is a subset of the scanned population, and the vacuity guard watches the population, not the subset — otherwise finishing the work would break the guard that protects it.
narrowed_at: 2026-08-28 (AT:R74) — 38 -> 21. Not a conversion: the census now distinguishes a CALL on a sync-I/O object from a mere mention of one.
cleared_at: 2026-11-22 (AT:B1) — 21 -> 0 (20 distinct handlers; room.py::event_stream appears twice in the census for its two nested generators). Also fixed, though the old census could not see them: games.py::trade and games.py::trade_quote ran a module-local `_require_ticker_or_422` (a DB session) directly on the loop. The census was tightened in the same change: it no longer treats a handler containing ANY run_in_threadpool call as clean, awaited/async-for calls are exempt, a hand-reviewed allowlist covers pure calls, and module-local sync helpers that open a session are followed one level.
